look_here_first: LOOK FIRST at a fully mature anthocarp under magnification: conspicuous stalked-glandular hairs and rounded longitudinal ribs favor B. coccinea. Then confirm perennial growth and leaves continuing up the stems; do not key from reddish flower color.

project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO records Texas as native at state scale; no project target-zone three-county PASS was established in completed review. Photo geography is not county occurrence evidence.

best_field_traits: Small clustered flowers and ribbed anthocarps; a petaloid perianth without a separate true corolla.
Mature anthocarps about 2.6–4 mm, densely stalked-glandular, with rounded ribs.
Perennial habit, leaves distributed along the stems; flower color is variable.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with B. erecta and B. linearifolia, mature B. coccinea fruits are densely stalked-glandular. B. erecta fruits are glabrous with sharp/acute ribs; B. linearifolia fruits are glabrous with broadly rounded ribs and smooth grooves. B. diffusa can resemble B. coccinea; compare multiple mature fruits and keyed characters before separating them.
